description: A comprehensive, industry-standard C Language learning roadmap from absolute beginner to systems architecture & low-level memory mastery level. Thoroughly covers C syntax, compiler pipeline, memory addresses, pointer arithmetic, structures, unions, dynamic memory allocation (malloc/free), file stream I/O, macro metaprogramming, bitwise operations, linked lists, stacks, queues, and capstone systems engineering projects.

institute.name: Coder & AccoTax
institute.author: Sukanta Hui
institute.location: 25(10/A) Shibtala Road, PO – N. C. Pukur, Barrackpore, West Bengal, India

subject: C Programming

teacher.name: Sukanta Hui
teacher.bio: Delivering deep systems intuition, pointer mastery, low-level memory efficiency, and industrial C programming fundamentals with clarity and hands-on lab rigor.

prerequisites: Basic computer literacy and mathematical aptitude
Understanding of how programs process data and store files
Willingness to debug runtime segfaults and think at the hardware level

segments.title: Segment 1 – C Language Fundamentals & Logic Building (Beginner)
segments.summary: Build a rock-solid C foundation: compiler compilation pipeline, tokens, primitive data types, operators, control flow branching, loops, functions, and call stack mechanics.

modules.title: Getting Started with C & Compiler Pipeline
modules.summary: Understand the origin of C, standards (K&R, C99, C11, C17), GCC compilation phases (Preprocessing, Compilation, Assembly, Linking), main function return codes, printf/scanf basics, and setting up the GCC environment.
topics: History and significance of C Language in modern systems programming
C standards evolution: K&R, ANSI C (C89/C90), C99, C11, C17, C23
Anatomy of GCC compilation pipeline: Source Code (.c) -> Preprocessor (.i) -> Compiler (.s) -> Assembler (.o) -> Linker (Executable)
Structure of a C program: include directives, global space, main() function, exit codes
Formatted Console I/O: printf(), scanf(), format specifiers (%d, %f, %c, %s)
Hands-on C Projects & Solutions for Module 001_001
Self-Test Module 001_001: 200 Comprehensive MCQs on C Foundations & Compiler Architecture
learningOutcomes: Explain how GCC compiles source code into native machine instructions
Write, compile, and debug standard C console applications
Format console output and parse user inputs accurately
commonMistakes: Forgetting & operator in scanf
Mismatched format specifiers
Forgetting return 0 in main
teachingTips: Demonstrate gcc -E, gcc -S, and gcc -c steps in terminal.

modules.title: C Tokens, Data Types & Operator Mechanics
modules.summary: Master C tokens, identifier rules, keywords, primitive data types (int, float, double, char, void), type modifiers (signed, unsigned, short, long), constants, bitwise operators, and sizeof operator mechanics.
topics: C Tokens breakdown: Keywords, Identifiers, Constants, Strings, Special Symbols, Operators
Fundamental data types & memory footprints across 32-bit and 64-bit architecture
Type Modifiers: short, long, signed, unsigned, and exact-width integer types (<stdint.h>)
Constants in C: #define preprocessor macros vs const keyword
Operator Precedence & Associativity: Arithmetic, Relational, Logical, Bitwise (&, |, ^, ~, <<, >>), Assignment, Ternary
Implicit type promotion vs explicit type casting
Hands-on C Projects & Solutions for Module 001_002
Self-Test Module 001_002: 200 Comprehensive MCQs on C Tokens, Data Types & Operators
learningOutcomes: Choose optimal data types and modifiers based on hardware constraints
Perform low-level bitwise operations and bit masking
Evaluate complex operator expressions without precedence bugs
commonMistakes: Integer overflow during arithmetic
Dividing two integers expecting float result without casting
teachingTips: Use hex and binary representations when explaining bitwise shift operators.
preReading: Binary number system and two's complement representation

modules.title: Control Flow: Branching, Decision Making & Loops
modules.summary: Master conditional decision-making (if, if-else, nested if, switch-case), loop constructs (while, do-while, for), jump statements (break, continue, goto), and complex algorithmic pattern logic.
topics: Conditional branching with if, else-if ladder, and nested decision trees
The switch-case statement: jump table optimization, fall-through behavior, break statement
Iterative loop constructs: while, do-while (post-test), for (pre-test)
Loop control mechanics: break, continue, and appropriate use of goto
Building nested loop algorithms: matrix indexing, prime detection, pyramid pattern printing
Hands-on C Projects & Solutions for Module 001_003
Self-Test Module 001_003: 200 Comprehensive MCQs on Control Flow, Branching & Loops
learningOutcomes: Construct robust control flow logic for conditional business processes
Optimize loop iterations and prevent infinite execution traps
Design nested loop algorithms for pattern generation and numeric testing
miniProjects: Interactive ATM Banking PIN & Menu Simulator
commonMistakes: Missing break statement in switch causing unintended fall-through
Using single '=' instead of '==' in condition
references: C Programming: A Modern Approach by K. N. King
teachingTips: Trace loop variables step-by-step on whiteboard with student scenarios.

modules.title: Functions, Scope & Storage Classes
modules.summary: Build modular C programs using function prototypes, parameters, call-by-value vs call-by-reference mechanics, variable scope rules, storage classes (auto, register, static, extern), and recursion call stack analysis.
topics: Modular design: Function declarations (prototypes), definitions, and invocation
Parameter passing mechanisms: Call by Value vs Passing Pointers for Call by Reference
Variable scope & lifetime: Local/Block scope vs Global/File scope
Storage Classes in C: auto, register, static (persistence across calls), extern (global linkage)
Recursion fundamentals: base condition, stack frames, call stack expansion, tail recursion
Hands-on C Projects & Solutions for Module 001_004
Self-Test Module 001_004: 200 Comprehensive MCQs on Functions, Scope & Storage Classes
learningOutcomes: Decompose complex programs into reusable, isolated function modules
Utilize static storage class for persistent state tracking without global variables
Write recursive functions with clear base cases to prevent stack overflow
miniProjects: Mathematical Recursion Toolkit (Fibonacci, GCD, Tower of Hanoi)
commonMistakes: Missing function prototype before main
Unbounded recursion causing Stack Overflow
teachingTips: Draw stack frame pushes and pops during recursive calls on board.

modules.title: C Pattern & Output Practice Lab
modules.summary: Master nested loops, coordinate geometry, C tokens, data types, operator precedence, bitwise logic, and evaluation rules with 60 hands-on C output practice questions.
topics: C Pattern Output Practice Lab: 20 Symmetrical, Pyramid, Number & Character Patterns
C Tokens, Data Types & Operators Output Practice Lab: 40 Tricky Questions & Explanations
Self Test 1: Segment 1 Comprehensive C Fundamentals Review (200 MCQs)
Segment 1 Capstone Projects: 10 Comprehensive C Systems & Algorithmic Projects
Project Pattern: 30 Comprehensive C Pattern Programs & Code Solutions
Project Series: 20 Comprehensive C Mathematical & Taylor Series Projects
learningOutcomes: Trace nested loop execution for 2D spatial coordinate mapping
Calculate leading spaces, odd star series, and boundary constraints
Predict and verify complex terminal ASCII pattern outputs
miniProjects: 20 Interactive C Pattern Output Practice Lab Questions
commonMistakes: Off-by-one errors in leading space loops
Missing newline printf(\n) after inner loop
references: C Programming: A Modern Approach by K. N. King
teachingTips: Show row (i) vs column (j) coordinate tables on whiteboard.

segments.title: Segment 2 – Arrays, Strings, Pointers & Memory Fundamentals (Intermediate)
segments.summary: Master contiguous memory allocation with 1D/2D arrays, null-terminated strings, string manipulation algorithms, memory addresses, pointer arithmetic, and function pointers.

modules.title: Arrays, Matrix Operations & Searching/Sorting
modules.summary: Deep dive into 1D, 2D (matrix), and multi-dimensional arrays in contiguous memory, array indexing, Linear Search, Binary Search, Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, Insertion Sort, and matrix algebra.
topics: 1D Array declaration, static memory allocation, contiguous memory layout, initialization
Passing arrays to functions: array decaying to pointer mechanism
Searching Algorithms: Linear Search vs Binary Search (time complexity analysis)
Sorting Algorithms in C: Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, Insertion Sort step-by-step implementation
2D Arrays & Matrices: Row-major order memory layout, matrix addition, transposition, and multiplication
Hands-on C Projects & Solutions for Module 002_005
Self-Test Module 002_005: 200 Comprehensive MCQs on Arrays, Searching, Sorting & Matrices
learningOutcomes: Manipulate 1D and 2D arrays in contiguous memory safely
Implement fundamental search and sort algorithms from scratch
Perform complex multi-dimensional matrix operations
commonMistakes: Out-of-bounds array access leading to undefined behavior
Off-by-one errors in loop boundaries
references: Data Structures using C by Reema Thareja
teachingTips: Draw physical RAM cell boxes showing contiguous addresses for array elements.

modules.title: Strings & Character Array Handling
modules.summary: Master null-terminated strings ('\0'), string input methods (gets_s, fgets, scanf), string formatting, string library functions (<string.h>), and custom string manipulation algorithms.
topics: Character arrays vs Null-terminated strings ('\0'): representation in memory
Safe String Input/Output: gets (deprecated) vs fgets(), puts(), and scanf %s pitfalls
Standard Library Functions (<string.h>): strlen, strcpy, strncpy, strcat, strcmp, strncmp, strchr, strstr
Custom String Manipulation: manual implementations of strlen, reverse, palindrome check, case conversion
Array of Strings (2D char arrays vs array of char pointers)
Hands-on C Projects & Solutions for Module 002_006
Self-Test Module 002_006: 200 Comprehensive MCQs on Strings & Character Array Handling
learningOutcomes: Process string data safely without buffer overflow vulnerabilities
Re-implement standard string header functions without relying on libraries
Manage 2D character arrays for text filtering and command processing
commonMistakes: Forgetting to allocate space for null terminator '\0'
Using '==' instead of strcmp() for string comparison
references: Secure Coding in C and C++ by Robert C. Seacord
teachingTips: Show buffer overflow attack concept when using gets vs fgets.

modules.title: Pointers, Address Arithmetic & Function Pointers
modules.summary: Master the heart of C: pointer variables, address-of (&) and dereference (*) operators, pointer arithmetic, array-pointer equivalence, pass-by-reference, double pointers (**), void pointers (void*), and function pointers.
topics: Pointer Fundamentals: Memory addresses, pointer variable declaration, initialization, null pointers (NULL)
Dereferencing (*) and Address-of (&) operators: accessing memory directly
Pointer Arithmetic: incrementing, decrementing, pointer subtraction, type scaling based on data type size
Pointer & Array Equivalence: subscripting arr[i] vs *(arr + i), passing pointers to functions
Pointers to Pointers (Double Pointers **): dynamic reference modification
Void Pointers (void*) & Type Casting: generic memory pointers
Function Pointers: declaration, assignment, callback functions, dispatch tables
Hands-on C Projects & Solutions for Module 002_007
Self-Test Module 002_007: 200 Comprehensive MCQs on Pointers, Address Arithmetic & Function Pointers
learningOutcomes: Manipulate memory addresses directly using pointer arithmetic
Pass pointer references to functions for in-place data mutation
Use function pointers to implement flexible callback architectures
miniProjects: Memory Address Inspector & In-place Array Inverter
commonMistakes: Dereferencing uninitialized or NULL pointers (Segfault)
Confusing pointer to const with const pointer
references: Pointers in C by Yashavant Kanetkar
Expert C Programming by Peter van der Linden
teachingTips: Draw RAM memory address maps (0x7fff...) showing pointer contents.

segments.title: Segment 3 – Derived Types, Dynamic Memory & File Handling (Advanced)
segments.summary: Master user-defined data structures with structs, unions, typedefs, memory alignment, dynamic memory allocation (malloc, calloc, realloc, free), and stream file I/O operations.

modules.title: Structures, Unions, Bit-fields & typedef
modules.summary: Group heterogeneous data types using struct, member access via dot (.) and arrow (->) operators, array of structures, memory padding & structure alignment, union memory sharing, bit-fields, and typedef type aliases.
topics: Structure declaration, member variables, initialization, and dot (.) access operator
Pointers to Structures & Arrow (->) operator: passing structs efficiently to functions
Array of Structures: managing multi-record datasets
Memory Alignment & Structure Padding: compiler padding rules, #pragma pack, sizeof(struct)
Unions: shared memory overlay, memory savings, type punning
Bit-fields: bit-level structure members for low-level protocol headers and hardware flag register packing
typedef keyword: creating meaningful type aliases for clean API signatures
Hands-on C Projects & Solutions for Module 003_008
learningOutcomes: Design composite structures for real-world domain models
Optimize struct layout to minimize compiler memory padding
Utilize unions and bit-fields for high-efficiency memory packing
commonMistakes: Confusing struct member access (.) with pointer member access (->)
Overwriting active union members unexpectedly
references: Understanding and Using C Pointers by Richard Reese
teachingTips: Calculate structure padding byte by byte on board.

modules.title: Dynamic Memory Allocation & Heap Management
modules.summary: Master heap memory management with malloc(), calloc(), realloc(), free(), detecting memory leaks, avoiding dangling pointers, double free errors, and allocating dynamic 2D arrays.
topics: Stack vs Heap Memory: static stack allocation vs dynamic heap lifetime
Dynamic allocation functions (<stdlib.h>): malloc() (uninitialized block), calloc() (zero-initialized array)
Resizing allocated memory: realloc() behavior, expanding/shrinking memory blocks safely
Deallocating memory with free(): returning heap memory to OS
Memory Management Hazards: Memory Leaks, Dangling Pointers, Double Free errors, Wild Pointers
Allocating Dynamic 2D Arrays: array of pointers vs single contiguous block
Hands-on C Projects & Solutions for Module 003_009
learningOutcomes: Allocate and manage dynamic heap memory safely at runtime
Prevent memory leaks and dangling pointer crashes in long-running apps
Construct dynamic resizable arrays and matrices on the heap
commonMistakes: Forgetting to call free() leading to memory leaks
Using freed pointer (dangling pointer access)
references: C Programming Language by Brian W. Kernighan
teachingTips: Demonstrate valgrind / memory analyzer output to catch leaks.
preReading: Operating system process memory layout (Text, Data, BSS, Heap, Stack)

modules.title: File Handling & Stream I/O Operations
modules.summary: Master file handling in C: streams (stdin, stdout, stderr), file pointer (FILE*), opening/closing modes (r, w, a, r+, w+, a+, rb, wb), text vs binary file operations (fgetc, fputc, fgets, fputs, fprintf, fscanf, fread, fwrite), and file positioning (fseek, ftell, rewind).
topics: Standard I/O Streams: stdin, stdout, stderr, and stream buffering
File Pointer (FILE*) & opening files with fopen(): read ('r'), write ('w'), append ('a'), update ('+') modes
Text File Operations: character I/O (fgetc/fputc), line I/O (fgets/fputs), formatted I/O (fprintf/fscanf)
Binary File Operations: raw block I/O with fread() and fwrite() for struct persistence
Random Access File Positioning: fseek(), ftell(), rewind(), SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, SEEK_END
Error handling in file streams: feof(), ferror(), clearing stream errors
Hands-on C Projects & Solutions for Module 003_010
learningOutcomes: Persist application data structures to disk using binary file streams
Parse formatted text log files and data feeds
Navigate file byte offsets randomly using fseek and ftell
commonMistakes: Forgetting to check if fopen returns NULL before reading/writing
Misunderstanding text vs binary mode line endings
references: Advanced Programming in the UNIX Environment by W. Richard Stevens
teachingTips: Inspect binary file contents in hex editor during class.

segments.title: Segment 4 – Preprocessor, Advanced C & Low-Level Systems Programming (Expert)
segments.summary: Master preprocessor macro metaprogramming, conditional compilation, multi-file build architectures, low-level data structures (Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues), command-line arguments, and production systems capstones.

modules.title: Preprocessor Directives & Macro Metaprogramming
modules.summary: Master the C preprocessor: macro definitions (#define), parameterised macro functions, operator stringizing (#), token concatenation (##), conditional compilation (#ifdef, #ifndef, #if, #elif, #else, #endif), header guards, and predefined macros (__FILE__, __LINE__, __DATE__, __TIME__).
topics: The Preprocessor Stage: text substitution before compilation
Object-like and Function-like Macros (#define): evaluation traps and parenthesization rules
Preprocessor Operators: Stringizing operator (#) and Token Concatenation operator (##)
Conditional Compilation: #ifdef, #ifndef, #if, #elif, #else, #endif for cross-platform support
Header Guards & #pragma once: preventing multiple inclusion bugs
Predefined Compiler Macros: __FILE__, __LINE__, __DATE__, __TIME__, __func__ for custom logging framework
Hands-on C Projects & Solutions for Module 004_011
learningOutcomes: Write safe, robust function-like macros without side-effect bugs
Implement cross-platform conditional compilation for Linux/Windows targets
Design automated logging and diagnostic macro frameworks
commonMistakes: Forgetting parentheses around macro parameters leading to precedence bugs
Missing header guards causing redefinition errors
teachingTips: Run gcc -E to show preprocessor output expansion.

modules.title: Data Structures & Systems Capstone Projects
modules.summary: Implement core data structures in pure C (Singly Linked List, Stack, Queue), handle command-line arguments (argc, argv), organize multi-file modular projects with Makefiles, and build production capstone systems.
topics: Implementing Singly Linked Lists in C: node structure, dynamic insertion, deletion, reversal, and traversal
Implementing Stack & Queue data structures using pointers and linked memory
Command-Line Arguments processing: argc, argv array parsing, flag handling
Multi-file Project Architecture: header (.h) vs implementation (.c) separation, linkage
Build Automation: introduction to Makefiles and build targets
Capstone Project: Full-featured C System Application with File Persistence and Memory Safety
Hands-on C Projects & Solutions for Module 004_012
learningOutcomes: Build custom data structures (Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues) from scratch in C
Develop multi-file modular C applications with header encapsulation
Write production-grade command-line systems software with persistent file storage
miniProjects: Command-Line File Utility & Linked List Manager
commonMistakes: Losing head pointer reference during linked list deletion causing memory leak
Off-by-one errors in argc index bounds
references: Algorithms in C by Robert Sedgewick
The Linux Programming Interface by Michael Kerrisk
teachingTips: Demonstrate full multi-file compilation and Makefile build workflow.
